abstract: ArXiv:2610.24041v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Low-order Carleman embeddings replace nonlinear dynamics by a larger linear system, but truncation errors can accumulate even when the underlying nonlinear model is accurately approximated by a quadratic equation. We construct a residual Carleman lift (RC2) of lattice Boltzmann dynamics in which an independently evolved spectral background supplies the coefficients and forcing of a second-order residual lift. In a double-shear-layer test, conventional fixed-rest Carleman reaches [MATH] final error, whereas prepared RC2 achieves [MATH] through vortex roll-up, without restarting the lift or using fine-reference feedback. The results demonstrate control of the finite-time accuracy of a fixed-order linear embedding through nonlinear preparation.
tldr: The paper develops a residual Carleman lift (RC2) to improve the finite-time accuracy of low-order linear embeddings of nonlinear lattice Boltzmann dynamics.
motivation: Low-order Carleman embeddings linearize nonlinear dynamics but suffer from truncation error accumulation, even when the underlying nonlinear model is well approximated by a quadratic equation.
method: An independently evolved spectral background supplies coefficients and forcing for a second-order residual lift of lattice Boltzmann dynamics, avoiding restarts or fine-reference feedback.
result: In a double-shear-layer test, the prepared RC2 reduces the final error dramatically compared with conventional fixed-rest Carleman, achieving accuracy through vortex roll-up.
conclusion: Nonlinear preparation can control the finite-time accuracy of a fixed-order linear embedding, demonstrating a practical route to more reliable Carleman-based simulations.

title: An Unbounded Gap Between Identification And Identifiable Elicitation: Central Moments
authors: Jingyi Jia
abstract: ArXiv:2610.24009v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For [MATH], two expectation equations identify the mean together with the [MATH]th central moment. How many coordinates must a report have if a one-observation loss uniquely elicits it and the report determines that moment? We prove that [MATH] coordinates are necessary and sufficient among all identifiable intermediaries. The result holds on every open convex set of positive distributions on any [MATH] distinct real outcomes. It requires no regularity of the loss, report map, identification function, or link. Thus [MATH] while [MATH], giving an unbounded gap between identifiable elicitation and indirect identification. This resolves the central-moment conjecture of Frongillo and Kash on the stated domains. The proof constructs a [MATH] manifold of supporting coefficients from the affine fibers of a convex negative Bayes risk. Translations along that manifold force an [MATH]-dimensional tangent space. Standardized moments of order at least three have the same exact complexity. The bound also extends to convex distribution classes with a full-dimensional raw-moment image.
tldr: The paper proves that eliciting the mean together with the k-th central moment requires exactly k+1 coordinates in an identifiable report, resolving the central-moment conjecture of Frongillo and Kash and establishing an unbounded gap between identifiable elicitation and indirect identification.
motivation: Property elicitation and identification functions are central to statistics and mechanism design, but the minimal report dimension needed for identifiable elicitation of central moments was previously unknown; the authors aim to settle this open conjecture.
method: The proof constructs a (k+2)-dimensional manifold of supporting coefficients from affine fibers of a convex negative Bayes risk function, and shows that translations along this manifold force a (k+1)-dimensional tangent space, working on arbitrary open convex sets of positive distributions over m distinct real outcomes without regularity assumptions.
result: Exactly k+1 coordinates are necessary and sufficient among all identifiable intermediaries, while indirect identification needs only 2, yielding an unbounded gap; the bound extends to standardized moments of order three and above and to convex distribution classes with full-dimensional raw-moment images.
conclusion: Identifiable elicitation can be fundamentally more demanding than indirect identification, and the central-moment conjecture is resolved on the stated domains with a fully general, regularity-free argument.

title: Orientation Diversity Provably Increases The Angular-Domain Rank Of 3d Mimo Arrays
authors: Elvino Sousa Samer Henry
abstract: ArXiv:2610.24228v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Movable and rotatable-antenna systems treat element placement as a design resource, but the supporting theory is largely position-only. We prove that element orientation is an effective spatial resource in its own right, complementary to position. For collinear or coplanar arrays, the angular-domain rank is capped by the number of projection-ambiguity classes of the scattering directions, for every common element orientation and pattern. Orientation-diverse elements with sufficiently rich analytic patterns restore the maximal rank min(N,L) for almost every orientation draw. A closed-form correlation expression, strictly monotone in orientation spread under isotropic scattering, quantifies the gain within the scalar-pattern model, and Monte Carlo simulations corroborate the exact-rank and capacity behavior.
tldr: The paper proves that element orientation diversity in movable/rotatable 3D MIMO antenna arrays raises the angular-domain rank, complementing position-only array design theory.
motivation: Movable and rotatable antenna systems treat element placement as a design resource, but existing theory accounts only for position, ignoring orientation as an independent spatial degree of freedom.
method: The authors derive rank bounds for collinear and coplanar arrays via projection-ambiguity classes of scattering directions, then prove that orientation-diverse elements with rich analytic patterns achieve maximal rank min(N,L) for almost every orientation draw, supported by a closed-form correlation expression and Monte Carlo simulations.
result: Angular-domain rank is capped by the number of projection-ambiguity classes for any common orientation, while orientation diversity restores maximal rank; the correlation expression is strictly monotone in orientation spread under isotropic scattering, and simulations confirm rank and capacity gains.
conclusion: Orientation should be treated as a first-class spatial design resource in 3D MIMO arrays, enabling provable rank and capacity improvements beyond position-only optimization.

title: A New Class Of Pyramidal Central Configurations For Spatial Newtonian 6-body Problems
authors: Liang Ding, Jin Wang, Jinrong Wang, Zhifu Xie
abstract: ArXiv:2610.24445v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While a non-concyclic rhombus can support a central configuration in the planar Newtonian four-body problem, such a configuration cannot serve as the base of a pyramidal central configuration in the spatial five-body problem. In this paper, we establish the existence of a new class of pyramidal central configurations in the spatial Newtonian six-body problem, characterized by a non-concyclic quadrilateral base. This geometric structure distinguishes the new configurations from the known pyramidal central configurations of the spatial five-body problem. We investigate several fundamental properties of these configurations and provide numerical examples illustrating the theoretical results in each case. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this new class of central configurations can be used to construct perverse solutions in three-dimensional space, revealing an additional connection between the geometry of central configurations and the dynamics of the Newtonian [MATH]-body problem.
tldr: The paper proves the existence of a new class of pyramidal central configurations for the spatial Newtonian six-body problem with a non-concyclic quadrilateral base.
motivation: Central configurations are fundamental in celestial mechanics, and known pyramidal constructions in the spatial five-body problem cannot use a non-concyclic rhombus base, motivating the search for new configurations in the six-body setting.
method: The authors construct and analyze pyramidal central configurations with a non-concyclic quadrilateral base, establish their existence, derive fundamental properties, and provide numerical examples.
result: A new class of spatial six-body pyramidal central configurations is shown to exist, distinguished geometrically from five-body pyramidal configurations, and these configurations are used to construct perverse solutions in three-dimensional space.
conclusion: The work reveals an additional connection between central-configuration geometry and the dynamics of the Newtonian N-body problem, though it lies outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Tree Plurality Veto: Voting In Few Rounds With Efficient Communication And Low Metric Distortion
authors: Gabriel Chen, Yu Cheng, Alice Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.24456v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the metric distortion framework for voting, where [MATH] voters and [MATH] candidates are embedded in an unknown metric space. A voting rule selects a candidate using only voters' ordinal preferences, and its distortion is the worst-case ratio between the social cost of the selected candidate and the minimum social cost. We study how round complexity trades off against total communication in deterministic voting protocols with low distortion. Deterministic rules can achieve the optimal distortion of [MATH] in one round by eliciting complete rankings using [MATH] bits, while a direct sequential implementation of PluralityVeto achieves the same distortion using only [MATH] bits but requires [MATH] rounds. Our main result is TreePluralityVeto, a deterministic voting protocol that, for every [MATH], achieves distortion at most [MATH] using at most [MATH] rounds and [MATH] bits of total communication, where [MATH]. The protocol runs PluralityVeto on a hierarchical partition of the voters, collecting restricted rankings in parallel at each level. The branching factor controls the tradeoff between rounds and communication, and a matching-based analysis shows that each level increases the distortion bound by at most [MATH].
tldr: The paper proposes TreePluralityVeto, a deterministic metric-distortion voting protocol that trades rounds against total communication.
motivation: Voting rules in metric distortion settings face a tradeoff between communication efficiency and round complexity, and the authors aim to achieve low distortion with few rounds and limited communication.
method: The protocol runs PluralityVeto on a hierarchical partition of voters, collecting restricted rankings in parallel at each level, with a branching factor controlling the rounds-communication tradeoff.
result: For every choice of parameters, TreePluralityVeto achieves distortion at most a specified bound using at most a certain number of rounds and bits of total communication, with each hierarchy level increasing distortion by at most a controlled amount.
conclusion: The work establishes a deterministic voting protocol that improves the round-communication tradeoff for low-distortion metric voting.

title: Heart Signal (ecg) As Vibration Signature For Human Authentication Using TinyML
authors: Yogeswar Reddy Thota, Student Member, IEEE, Hanan Alsmadi, Student Member, IEEE, Tooraj Nikoubin, Senior Member, IEEE
abstract: ArXiv:2610.24761v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ensuring data security in the era of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and deepfake technology requires robust biometric systems. Conventional methods such as facial recognition, iris scans, fingerprints, and voice recognition are increasingly vulnerable to spoofing and provide only one-time authentication at login. This study introduces an Electrocardiogram (ECG) based authentication framework, compared with Photoplethysmography (PPG), leveraging Tiny Machine Learning (TinyML) for deployment on resource-constrained microcontroller units (MCUs). The proposed method enables continuous authentication, offering ongoing verification throughout device usage, which conventional biometrics cannot achieve. It also serves as a password-free solution, reducing risks of credential loss, theft, or reuse. However, ECG signals vary with physical activity, health conditions, age, and emotional states, requiring robust signal processing and learning algorithms. To address this, efficient TinyML models were designed to mitigate recognition errors from noisy real-time data. Experiments used single-lead ECG signals (Lead I) from UofTDB, MIT-BIH Arrhythmia, MIT-BIH Noise Stress Test, and PTB databases. Spectrograms and spectral features were extracted to train Deep Neural Network (DNN), 1D CNN, and 2D CNN models within the Edge Impulse platform, achieving 98% accuracy. The trained model was converted into TinyML format and deployed on an Espressif ESP-EYE (ESP32, 240 MHz). Support Vector Machine (SVM) models were also applied for benchmarking. By analyzing the number of heartbeats required for reliable recognition, the results show that averaging multiple signals improves tolerance to noise and enhances accuracy. Overall, ECG-based authentication demonstrates strong potential as a secure, real-time, and continuously verifiable method for personal identification on wearable and edge devices.
tldr: The paper proposes an ECG-based continuous biometric authentication framework using TinyML models deployed on resource-constrained microcontrollers.
motivation: Conventional biometrics such as face, iris, fingerprint, and voice are vulnerable to spoofing and typically provide only one-time login authentication, motivating continuous and password-free alternatives.
method: The authors extract spectrograms and spectral features from single-lead ECG signals across several public databases and train DNN, 1D CNN, and 2D CNN models in Edge Impulse, then deploy the converted TinyML model on an ESP32-based ESP-EYE board, with SVM benchmarking.
result: The TinyML models achieve up to 98% accuracy, and averaging multiple heartbeat signals is shown to improve noise tolerance and recognition reliability.
conclusion: ECG-based authentication is presented as a promising secure, real-time, continuously verifiable biometric method for wearable and edge devices.

title: Modeling The Coevolution Of Human Skills And Ai Adoption
authors: Giacomo Frigerio, Susanna Caruso, Giacomo Livan, Vito Latora
abstract: ArXiv:2610.24794v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The value of relying on generative AI depends on two quantities that evolve with its use: users' unaided skill, which may decline without practice, and the originality of AI-assisted work, which may decline as more people rely on similar tools. We model this process as a coevolutionary game in which individuals choose between autonomous and AI-assisted work, with autonomous practice strengthening their skills while reliance on AI gradually erodes them. When the reinforcing effect of skill erosion outweighs the crowding cost of lost originality, the population exhibits two alternative stable states: low AI adoption with high average skill, and high AI adoption with low average skill. Because skill is individual, autonomous workers remain more skilled than AI users, making autonomous work less vulnerable to population-wide skill decline. The strength of this effect is governed by a timescale ratio: the rate at which skills adapt relative to the rate at which individuals change strategy. The same ratio determines the full distribution of skills, which we derive analytically. Populations with identical AI adoption and average skill can differ sharply: when strategies change frequently, skills remain homogeneous and collective lock-in to high AI adoption is stronger; when strategies persist, lock-in weakens but the population can polarize into highly skilled autonomous workers and AI-dependent individuals. Modeling output overlap further shows that more diverse AI outputs can make widespread adoption harder to reverse. Together, these results expose tradeoffs between the benefits of widespread AI adoption and its long-run risks, making collective lock-in and skill polarization distinct intervention targets.
tldr: A coevolutionary game-theoretic model shows that AI adoption and users' unaided skills can co-evolve into two alternative stable states—high adoption/low skill or low adoption/high skill—depending on a timescale ratio between skill adaptation and strategy switching.
motivation: The authors aim to capture two coupled quantities that change with generative-AI use: the erosion of unaided human skill through disuse, and the decline in originality of AI-assisted work as adoption becomes widespread.
method: Individuals choose between autonomous and AI-assisted work in a population game; autonomous practice strengthens skill while AI reliance erodes it, and output-overlap (crowding) costs reduce the value of AI-assisted originality. The skill distribution is derived analytically as a function of the ratio between skill-adaptation and strategy-switching rates.
result: When skill-erosion reinforcement outweighs the crowding cost of lost originality, the population exhibits bistability between low-adoption/high-skill and high-adoption/low-skill states; fast strategy switching homogenizes skills and strengthens lock-in, whereas persistent strategies weaken lock-in but can polarize the population into highly skilled autonomous workers and AI-dependent users.
conclusion: Collective lock-in and skill polarization emerge as distinct intervention targets, and greater diversity of AI outputs can make widespread adoption harder to reverse, exposing tradeoffs between the benefits and long-run risks of AI adoption.

title: Build Your Own Neural Network From Scratch
authors: Samantha Donner, Ethan Geary, Peter March, Mathew Umano
abstract: ArXiv:2610.24271v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: These notes are based on our reading of Michael Nielsen's online book neuralnetworksanddeeplearning.com. They represent our effort to elaborate his exposition of neural networks and to provide supporting mathematical detail. Our goal is to provide self-contained instructions for building a basic neural network in the form of pseudocode, so that an interested reader can build a network from scratch and know why it works. No prior knowledge of neural networks or of Python is assumed. Some familiarity with linear algebra, calculus, and probability is helpful but we explain the relevant mathematics in a set of appendices designed to be accessible to newcomers.
tldr: These are self-contained tutorial notes for building a basic neural network from scratch, based on Michael Nielsen's online book.
motivation: The authors aim to elaborate Nielsen's exposition with supporting mathematical detail so that newcomers can implement and understand a simple neural network.
method: The notes provide pseudocode instructions and appendices covering relevant linear algebra, calculus, and probability for readers without prior neural network or Python experience.
result: The outcome is a pedagogical, self-contained guide to constructing a basic neural network and understanding why it works.
conclusion: The paper is an educational tutorial in classical neural networks and has no direct connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Minimality Of $T_z^*$-Invariant Subspaces Of $H^2(\mathbb D^2)$
authors: Marcos S. Ferreira Jo\~ao Marcos R. Do Carmo
abstract: ArXiv:2610.24327v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish necessary conditions for the minimality of infinite-dimensional [MATH]-invariant subspaces of [MATH]. More precisely, we prove that if [MATH] is an infinite-dimensional, minimal [MATH]-invariant subspace, then, for every [MATH], either [MATH] or [MATH] where [MATH] is an atomic singular inner function and [MATH] denotes the orthogonal projection of [MATH] onto [MATH]. As [MATH] is a universal operator on [MATH], this result reduces the Invariant Subspace Problem to the analysis of these two alternatives for infinite-dimensional minimal [MATH]-invariant subspaces.
tldr: The paper derives necessary conditions for minimality of infinite-dimensional Tz*-invariant subspaces of the Hardy space H^2(D^2) on the bidisc, reducing the Invariant Subspace Problem to two structural alternatives.
motivation: The Invariant Subspace Problem remains a central open problem in operator theory; the authors exploit the fact that the Tz* operator is universal on H^2(D^2) to constrain the possible minimal infinite-dimensional invariant subspaces.
method: Pure complex analysis and operator theory: the authors analyze Tz*-invariant subspaces and their orthogonal projections, employing atomic singular inner functions and inner-outer factorization techniques on the bidisc.
result: They prove that for every point in the unit bidisc, a minimal infinite-dimensional Tz*-invariant subspace must satisfy one of two explicit alternatives involving an atomic singular inner function and the associated orthogonal projection.
conclusion: The classification narrows the Invariant Subspace Problem to the study of these two alternatives, providing new necessary conditions in the multivariable setting.

title: Benign Overfitting Property Of The Minimum $\ell_q$ -norm Interpolant Estimator In Regression Problem Via Feature Space Decomposition
authors: Rados{\l}aw Adamczak, Guillaume Lecu\'e, Zong Shang, Marta Strzelecka
abstract: ArXiv:2610.24350v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper establishes high-probability, non-asymptotic upper bounds for the population excess risk of minimum [MATH]-norm interpolating estimators in linear regression, valid for all [MATH] under three scenarios: convex concentration, mild moment assumptions and log-concavity. Consequently, we derive sufficient conditions for these estimators to exhibit benign overfitting. Our analysis hinges on a Feature Space Decomposition (FSD) framework, which naturally highlights the self-regularizing properties of minimum norm interpolants as well as the role of alignment between the signal and the features for benign overfitting. From a technical perspective, our approach circumvents the traditionally used Convex Gaussian Min-max Theorem (CGMT) by instead leveraging the Dvoretzky-Milman theorem. We emphasize that the FSD method has the potential to refine standard uniform convergence approaches. Furthermore, the isomorphic Dvoretzky-Milman theorem established herein -- proven under the three scenarios mentioned above -- for the [MATH]-norm is of independent mathematical interest.
tldr: The paper derives high-probability non-asymptotic excess risk bounds for minimum ℓ_q-norm interpolating estimators in linear regression via a Feature Space Decomposition framework, giving sufficient conditions for benign overfitting.
motivation: Minimum-norm interpolants can generalize well despite perfect fitting, and existing analyses rely heavily on the Convex Gaussian Min-max Theorem; the authors aim for a more general and transparent treatment valid for all q and weaker distributional assumptions.
method: They introduce a Feature Space Decomposition that isolates the self-regularizing effect of minimum-norm interpolants and the signal-feature alignment, replacing CGMT with an isomorphic Dvoretzky-Milman theorem proved under convex concentration, mild moment, and log-concavity scenarios.
result: They obtain non-asymptotic high-probability upper bounds on population excess risk for all ℓ_q norms and derive sufficient conditions under which benign overfitting occurs, with the Dvoretzky-Milman result being of independent mathematical interest.
conclusion: The FSD approach offers a unified, assumption-flexible route to benign overfitting analysis and may refine standard uniform convergence arguments in high-dimensional statistics.

title: Spherical-Design Oracles For Zeroth-Order Optimisation: Deterministic, Variance-Free Gradient Estimation
authors: Amir Ali Farzin, Yuen-Man Pun, Philipp Braun, Iman Shames
abstract: ArXiv:2610.24373v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we develop a zeroth-order (ZO) method that estimates the gradient with minimal bias and variance. Instead of the random directions often used in the ZO literature, we consider central differences with directions given by a fixed spherical [MATH]-design, a finite point set that integrates every polynomial of degree at most [MATH] exactly. The oracle is deterministic and thus does not induce any variance.We also propose a general finite difference method in the higher-order-smoothness regime and show the bias of both finite difference methods. We then show the convergence of the proposed ZO method via the input-to-state stability concept. Numerical experiments show the superiority of our proposed method over the existing random ZO methods.
tldr: A deterministic zeroth-order gradient estimator built on fixed spherical designs that eliminates variance in derivative-free optimisation.
motivation: Random-direction zeroth-order methods suffer from high variance in gradient estimates, so the authors seek a deterministic, variance-free alternative.
method: Central finite differences are taken along directions from a fixed spherical t-design, with bias analysed for both first-order and higher-order smoothness regimes and convergence proved via input-to-state stability.
result: Bias bounds are derived for the design-based finite-difference schemes, and numerical experiments show improved performance over randomised zeroth-order baselines.
conclusion: Spherical-design oracles offer a practical deterministic route to low-bias, variance-free gradient estimation, though the work is purely classical optimisation with no quantum information, thermodynamic, network, or hybrid-platform content.

title: The Segal-Bargmann Transform In Neural Partial Differential Equations
authors: Jie Xu, Julio Castrill\'on-Cand\'as, Mark Kon, Qinxun Bai
abstract: ArXiv:2610.24497v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a novel neural operator method based on Segal-Bargmann transform and Bargmann-Fock space for learning the solution operators of partial differential equations (PDEs). The method brings data encoding, latent-space representation, operator learning, and decoding into an unifed framework. From only finitely many observations, we establish a sup-norm reconstruction error of order [MATH], where L is the number of complex sampling points that are decoupled with the original samplings and observations. The reconstruction error is independent of the spatial dimension and the number of original sampling points. We show that this new mesh-free Segal-Bargmann Neural Operator approach has superior performance compared to existing NO approaches like FNO, BelNet, GNOT, etc.,\ particularly in terms of pointwise control [MATH] for solutions of PDEs [MATH] which provides pointwise accuracy and interpretability as classical numerical solvers. We also demonstrates the reconstructions of the solution operators for higher dimensional nonlinear PDEs, which suggest that our proposed method has great potential to be applied to more challenging PDEs and to even higher spatial dimensions.
tldr: The paper introduces a mesh-free neural operator based on the Segal-Bargmann transform and Bargmann-Fock space for learning solution operators of PDEs, with dimension-independent sup-norm reconstruction error guarantees and superior pointwise accuracy compared with FNO, BelNet, and GNOT.
motivation: Existing neural operator approaches for PDEs often lack pointwise accuracy guarantees and interpretability comparable to classical numerical solvers, and their error bounds can degrade with spatial dimension.
method: Data encoding, latent representation, operator learning, and decoding are unified within Bargmann-Fock space using the Segal-Bargmann transform, yielding a mesh-free neural operator whose reconstruction error is controlled by the number of complex sampling points and is independent of spatial dimension and original sample count.
result: The approach achieves a sup-norm reconstruction error bound independent of dimension and sampling count, and empirically outperforms FNO, BelNet, and GNOT, particularly in pointwise control, including for higher-dimensional nonlinear PDEs.
conclusion: The Segal-Bargmann neural operator offers accurate, interpretable, mesh-free PDE operator learning with strong potential for challenging high-dimensional problems, though it lies outside quantum information science.

title: Skew-Symmetric Formulations And Energy-Stable Schemes For Compressible Reactive Flow Equations
authors: Weifeng Zhao Junbo Gong
abstract: ArXiv:2610.24524v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops skew-symmetric formulations and energy stable finite difference schemes for the reactive Euler and reactive Navier--Stokes equations. By introducing suitable transformed variables, we rewrite the governing equations into skew-symmetric forms and obtain continuous energy estimates by standard integration-by-parts arguments. The proposed formulations extend the skew-symmetric framework for compressible flow equations to reactive systems, where the chemical energy and the species equation must be incorporated into the transformed variables. Based on these formulations, we construct semi-discrete schemes with summation-by-parts (SBP) operators. The convective terms are discretized by the non-dissipative part of linear upwind SBP operators, while a nonlinear SBP--WENO operator is used only to supply artificial dissipation near discontinuities. For periodic boundary conditions, the resulting schemes satisfy semi-discrete energy estimates consistent with the continuous analysis. Numerical experiments in one and two space dimensions validate the designed order of accuracy and demonstrate stable performance for problems with shocks, viscous layers, detonation-type waves, and complex wave interactions.
tldr: The paper develops skew-symmetric formulations and energy-stable finite-difference (SBP) schemes for compressible reactive Euler and Navier-Stokes equations.
motivation: Extending provably energy-stable, skew-symmetric numerical frameworks from compressible flow to reactive systems requires incorporating chemical energy and species equations into transformed variables.
method: Transformed variables recast the governing equations in skew-symmetric form, yielding continuous energy estimates via integration by parts; semi-discrete schemes use summation-by-parts operators with linear upwind SBP for convection and a nonlinear SBP-WENO operator for artificial dissipation near discontinuities.
result: The schemes satisfy semi-discrete energy estimates consistent with the continuous analysis under periodic boundary conditions, and 1D/2D numerical experiments confirm design accuracy and stability for shocks, viscous layers, detonation waves, and complex wave interactions.
conclusion: The skew-symmetric framework successfully extends to reactive flows, providing robust energy-stable schemes for detonation and shock-dominated problems.

title: Analytical Methods For Solving Non-Autonomous Higher-Order Nonlinear Difference Equations
authors: Tshifhiwa Murovhi, Mensah Folly-Gbetoula, Kwassi Anani
abstract: ArXiv:2610.24657v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A system of four-dimensional fifth-order rational difference equations with variable coefficients is considered. The method employed is the well-known Lie symmetry analysis initially developed for differential equations. Linearised symmetry conditions are applied, reduction operators are introduced, functional equations are solved, and symmetry generators are derived. The admitted point symmetries are then used to construct closed-form solutions. This work is a non-autonomous generalisation of autonomous fifth-order rational systems in the literature.
tldr: The paper applies Lie symmetry analysis to construct closed-form solutions of a non-autonomous four-dimensional system of fifth-order rational difference equations with variable coefficients.
motivation: Autonomous fifth-order rational difference systems have known solutions, and this work extends such solvability to the non-autonomous (variable-coefficient) case, which is substantially harder.
method: Linearised symmetry conditions are derived, reduction operators introduced, functional equations solved, and symmetry generators obtained via Lie point symmetry analysis originally developed for differential equations.
result: Admitted point symmetries are identified and used to build explicit closed-form solutions for the variable-coefficient system.
conclusion: The approach generalises prior autonomous results and offers a systematic symmetry-based route to solving higher-order nonlinear difference equations.

title: Recording-Aware Evaluation Of Multimodal Ot Intrusion Detection
authors: Mustafa Umut Ozbek, Khalil El-Khatib, Li Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.24128v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine-learning-based intrusion detection systems (IDSs) for operational technology (OT) are commonly evaluated on benchmark datasets in which normal and attack data are collected in separate recordings. In such settings, high performance may reflect recording-associated differences as well as attack behavior. We introduce a recording-aware evaluation procedure that compares attack windows with background from the same recording, uses prior data for model fitting and calibration, tests temporal alignment against randomized event schedules, and reports event coverage together with alarm burden. On the ProvICS multimodal dataset, cyber modalities strongly distinguish the benign and attack recordings before the first labeled attack. Same-recording evaluation reverses the apparent modality ranking across all studied window sizes: the physical view becomes the strongest individual modality, while cyber-only fusion shows the largest difference between cross-recording and same-recording AUC, reaching 0.54. Operational analysis further shows that permissive event-overlap metrics can overstate detection when a small number of long alarm episodes cover multiple actions. An external analysis on HAI shows smaller and reference-dependent recording sensitivity. These findings show that cross-recording benchmark performance should be interpreted alongside same-recording, forward, temporal, and operational evaluations.
tldr: The paper proposes a recording-aware evaluation procedure for machine-learning-based operational technology intrusion detection and shows that cross-recording benchmarks can inflate or distort modality rankings.
motivation: Many OT intrusion-detection benchmarks mix normal and attack data across separate recordings, so high performance may reflect recording artifacts rather than attack behavior.
method: The authors introduce same-recording evaluation, forward model fitting/calibration, temporal-alignment tests against randomized schedules, and operational metrics for event coverage and alarm burden, applied to ProvICS and HAI.
result: On ProvICS, cyber modalities strongly separate benign and attack recordings before the first labeled attack; same-recording evaluation reverses modality rankings, with physical modalities strongest and cyber-only fusion showing a 0.54 AUC gap.
conclusion: Cross-recording benchmark performance should be interpreted alongside same-recording, forward, temporal, and operational evaluations to avoid overstating detection capability.

title: Can Agents Keep Secrets They Were Never Told? Benchmarking Latent Privacy Risks Across Sessions With MemJoin
authors: Qishun Yang, Shu Yang, Difei Xu, Di Wang, Meng Ding
abstract: ArXiv:2610.24359v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: To support sustained interactions and personalized assistance, agents use long-term memory to retain and combine user information across sessions. Reusing such memories can lead an agent to state a sensitive relation while completing an ordinary task that does not require it. The relation to protect and the combination of clues that reveal it may remain hidden at memory write time, when later records and tasks are still unknown. In this paper, we introduce MemJoin, a privacy benchmark of 288 synthetic analysis cases in which the complete history entails a sensitive relation, but every individual session is insufficient. We evaluate six memory systems with the same answer-generating model, alongside full-history and no-history controls. Each system writes and updates memories in session order and later retrieves context for an ordinary task, while target annotations remain with the evaluator. We separately check which target attribute values appear in stored records and retrieved context, and whether the final answer states the complete, person-linked relation. In a separate paired test on a prespecified subset, removing shared identifiers and other connecting clues can change complete-relation output while all checked target attribute values remain visible. These findings show why checking attribute visibility alone is insufficient to evaluate what records from different sessions reveal together.
tldr: MemJoin is a 288-case synthetic benchmark testing whether LLM agents with cross-session memory leak sensitive relations that are only inferable from the combination of individually innocuous sessions.
motivation: Long-term memory lets agents combine user information across sessions, so a sensitive relation may become statable even though no single session contains it and the relation was never explicitly disclosed.
method: Six memory systems sharing one answer-generating model are compared against full-history and no-history controls; memories are written and updated in session order, then retrieved for an ordinary task, with separate checks on attribute visibility versus complete person-linked relation output, plus a paired ablation removing shared identifiers.
result: Checking whether target attribute values appear in stored records or retrieved context is insufficient; removing shared identifiers can change complete-relation output while all checked attribute values remain visible.
conclusion: Privacy evaluation of memory-enabled agents must assess what records jointly reveal across sessions, not merely per-record attribute visibility.

title: Llm Trojans That Increase Response Lengths And Cost
authors: Zhengxing Li, Guangmingmei Yang, Nader Alfares, David J. Miller, George Kesidis
abstract: ArXiv:2610.24784v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Management of the token-based costs of using LLMs has emerged as a significant problem. Some frontier-model providers charge five times per response token than per prompt token, while others offer prefilling discounts for prompt tokens. In this paper, we devise a defense against a new data-poisoning attack that plants a Trojan which increases the length of the response (and hence the cost to the user) when its trigger is present in the prompt. In particular, we demonstrate how a subtle Trojan may trigger on semantically similar instructions of an instruction fine-tuned LLM.
tldr: The paper introduces a defense against a data-poisoning Trojan attack that covertly lengthens LLM responses to inflate token-based usage costs.
motivation: Token-based pricing of frontier LLMs makes response-length inflation a financially motivated attack surface, and no existing defense addresses adversarially induced verbosity.
method: The authors construct a subtle Trojan trigger embedded via instruction fine-tuning on semantically similar instructions, then devise and evaluate a detection/mitigation defense against it.
result: They show that a Trojan can reliably trigger longer responses on semantically similar prompts, and that their proposed defense can detect or suppress the malicious behavior.
conclusion: Response-length Trojans are a practical cost-inflation threat to deployed LLMs, and targeted defenses can mitigate them, though robustness across models remains to be established.

title: Same Data, Different Bytes: Serialization-Invariant Integrity Checks For Agent-Published Datasets
authors: Maura Clark Jin Gao
abstract: ArXiv:2610.24916v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent networks require reliable ways for requesting agents to verify where data is located, how it can be accessed, and whether the data received matches what the data owner made available. Checksum mismatches can reflect either altered content or serialization differences that preserve data equivalence under specified rules. Data identification mechanisms for agents, such as DataFacts, describe where data can be accessed and provide checksums for checking received data against published references. We propose a serialization-invariant identification method that assigns the same identifier to data representations equivalent under explicit rules. We use DataFacts as a case study, retaining its existing checksum alongside the proposed identifier. In a controlled agent study, we compare the proposed configuration with ordinary-tool and checksum baselines across equivalent re-encodings, altered content, and unavailable references. The study includes three model tiers from each of two providers. For equivalent re-encodings, the proposed configuration increased expected-outcome rates by 80.4 percentage points over the ordinary-tool baseline and by 70.2 percentage points over the checksum baseline. The proposed configuration also increased evidence-supported rejection of altered content by 3.5 percentage points over the checksum baseline. We contribute a serialization-invariant identification method with explicit equivalence rules, an integration approach illustrated through DataFacts, and an empirical evaluation against ordinary-tool and checksum baselines.
tldr: The paper proposes a serialization-invariant identifier for agent-published datasets so equivalent data encodings receive the same identifier while altered content is still detectable.
motivation: Agent networks need reliable data identification and integrity verification, but ordinary checksums conflate semantically equivalent re-serializations with actual content changes.
method: Using DataFacts as a case study, the authors define equivalence rules and add a serialization-invariant identifier alongside existing checksums, then evaluate it in a controlled agent study across model tiers and providers.
result: The proposed configuration improved expected-outcome rates by 80.4 percentage points over an ordinary-tool baseline and 70.2 points over a checksum baseline for equivalent re-encodings, with a modest 3.5-point gain in rejecting altered content.
conclusion: Serialization-invariant identification improves dataset integrity checks for agent networks, though the work is empirical systems research and not aligned with quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Many Repairs, One Direction: Steering Code Models Toward Safer Cryptographic Api Use
authors: Tianhe Lu, Sakuna Harinda Jayasundara, Eric Spero, Ewan Tempero, Robert Biddle, Giovanni Russello
abstract: ArXiv:2610.25133v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cryptographic API misuse in large language model-generated code can compromise software security. While many existing approaches improve code security by modifying model parameters or inputs, how representation changes associated with different cryptographic API repairs can support a shared intervention for safer code generation remains underexplored. To investigate this, we construct 48,000 matched program pairs across four programming languages and ten cryptographic API misuse categories. Each pair changes a specified API decision while preserving the programming task. Subtracting the misuse program's internal representation from its secure counterpart's gives a repair vector. Across five models, comparisons of mean repair vectors reveal stronger organization by misuse category than by language. These category-specific patterns also support a shared intervention. We introduce CrypSteer, which extracts a shared direction by normalizing repair differences and selecting a principal component aligned with repairs across misuse categories. With model weights fixed, adding one shared direction per model to its internal activations during generation improves aggregate target security rates by 5.28--15.00 percentage points over unsteered generation across languages and misuse categories. These findings connect the shared structure of cryptographic repair representations to a reusable intervention for safer code generation.
tldr: The paper introduces CrypSteer, a representation-steering intervention that extracts a single shared activation direction to make LLM-generated code use cryptographic APIs more securely.
motivation: Cryptographic API misuse in LLM-generated code is a real security risk, and existing fixes rely on retraining or input modification; the authors ask whether the internal representation differences between insecure and secure code versions share enough structure to permit one reusable intervention.
method: They build 48,000 matched program pairs across four languages and ten cryptographic misuse categories, compute 'repair vectors' as differences of internal representations, and extract a shared direction via normalized repair differences and a principal component aligned across categories, which is added to activations at inference time with frozen weights.
result: Mean repair vectors cluster more strongly by misuse category than by language, and the single shared direction per model raises aggregate target security rates by 5.28-15.00 percentage points over unsteered generation across five models.
conclusion: Shared representational structure underlies distinct cryptographic repairs, enabling a lightweight, weight-free steering intervention for safer code generation.

title: Peer Pressure: Execution-Verified Co-Evolution Of Attacker And Defender Populations For Code Security
authors: Khushbu Pahwa, Yubin Ge, Daniele Bonadiman, Xiaofei Ma, Yi Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.24896v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM code agents increasingly ship code with little oversight, yet defenders trained on static vulnerability datasets fall behind adapting adversaries. We co-train attacker and defender instead, and let execution decide every reward: an attacker (Red) edits a real repository and earns nothing unless its patch applies, builds, passes the tests, completes its development task and reproduces a real exploit in an isolated container, whose path also labels the entry point, the critical operation and the trace between them. Peer-Relative Policy Optimization (PRPO) makes both sides populations of LoRA adapters over one frozen base and credits each against same-role peers that faced an identical condition, placing the population inside the policy-gradient baseline rather than the opponent pool, with a tournament preserving diversity. Matching cancels the condition's difficulty: at equal coverage it is worth 2.3 points of balanced accuracy over a baseline computed on other conditions, and it matches a within-policy control at half the verifier spend. PRPO's 7B diff reviewer reaches 64.8% balanced accuracy on four unseen applications in three untrained languages, 5.5 points above supervised security fine-tuning and 4.4 above a frozen frontier reviewer (Claude Opus 4.8), which it leads by 15.8 on the application it trains on. Its 9B repository agent recovers 23 of 172 held-out VulnGym advisories, against 10 after supervised fine-tuning and 7 for the same backbone untrained under the same scaffold, and locates 17 of 43 reachable entry points against 13 for mini-swe-agent with GLM-5.2. Run unchanged on jailbreak defense, the same algorithm matches or exceeds WildGuard's static F1 at equal corpus and model size. Under a judge distinct from its training oracle it cuts attack success from 36.0% to 4.6%, against WildGuard's 8.9%.
tldr: The paper co-trains LLM-based attacker and defender populations for code security using execution-verified rewards and a peer-relative policy optimization method.
motivation: LLM code agents increasingly generate code with little oversight, while defenders trained on static vulnerability datasets struggle against adaptive adversaries.
method: The authors co-evolve Red (attacker) and Blue (defender) populations of LoRA adapters over a frozen base model, using execution in isolated containers to verify patches, builds, tests, exploits, and labels, and introduce Peer-Relative Policy Optimization (PRPO) to credit agents against same-role peers under matched conditions.
result: PRPO's 7B diff reviewer reaches 64.8% balanced accuracy on unseen applications and languages, outperforming supervised security fine-tuning and a frozen frontier reviewer; the 9B repository agent recovers 23 of 172 held-out advisories and also improves jailbreak defense robustness.
conclusion: Execution-verified population co-evolution with PRPO provides a stronger and more adaptive code-security training paradigm than static supervised fine-tuning, with transfer to related security tasks.

title: SoK: PIAtlas: Decomposing The Unbounded Prompt Injection Attack Space
authors: Konstantinos Psounis Stavros Damianakis
abstract: ArXiv:2610.24999v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Prompt injection is the dominant security risk for large-language-model (LLM) applications and agents, yet the field still lacks a coherent map of how these attacks are constructed. More than twenty public datasets describe prompt injection using incompatible vocabularies, often organized around delivery vector, attacker goal, or generation method. In this Systematization of Knowledge, we present PIAtlas, a taxonomy organized instead around how the injected instruction is constructed to subvert the underlying model. Its six classes, one per subversion mechanism, form the roots of a hierarchy of techniques and sub-techniques that researchers can use to describe attacks consistently and design more systematic evaluations. We derive the taxonomy from how LLMs are trained, prompted, and influenced by human-like framing, and compare it with historical attack data. To ground this comparison, we release PICorpus, to our knowledge the largest license-clean collection of public prompt-injection datasets, and map thousands of its records to PIAtlas under a human-verified protocol. The mapping shows that attacks usually combine several techniques drawn from only a few mechanisms. It also reveals gaps that existing labels obscure: widely used agent benchmarks test only part of the attack space, and adaptive attackers favor mechanisms that curated benchmarks underrepresent. PIAtlas thus provides a common foundation for understanding this attack space, improving benchmark coverage, and guiding red teaming and defenses.
tldr: PIAtlas is a Systematization of Knowledge that taxonomizes prompt-injection attacks against LLM applications by how the injected instruction is constructed to subvert the model, backed by a large curated corpus (PICorpus) of public datasets.
motivation: Prompt injection is the dominant security risk for LLM applications, yet existing datasets and benchmarks use incompatible vocabularies organized around delivery vector, attacker goal, or generation method, leaving no coherent map of the attack space.
method: The authors derive a six-class taxonomy rooted in how LLMs are trained, prompted, and influenced by human-like framing, then release PICorpus, the largest license-clean collection of public prompt-injection datasets, and map thousands of records to the taxonomy under a human-verified protocol.
result: The mapping shows attacks typically combine several techniques drawn from only a few mechanisms, that widely used agent benchmarks cover only part of the attack space, and that adaptive attackers favor mechanisms which curated benchmarks underrepresent.
conclusion: PIAtlas provides a common descriptive foundation for the prompt-injection space, aiming to improve benchmark coverage and guide red teaming and defenses.

title: T-embeddings As Stationary Measures On T-graphs
authors: Mikhail Basok, Benoit Laslier, Marianna Russkikh
abstract: ArXiv:2610.24180v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the relation between t-embeddings and T-graphs associated with the same weighted planar bipartite graph. We prove that, given such a T-graph, the corresponding t-embeddings are classified by positive stationary measures on this T-graph and describe a reconstruction procedure of the t-embedding given such a measure. As an application, we develop an approach for constructing t-embeddings of arbitrary sufficiently non-degenerate planar bipartite graphs.
tldr: The paper establishes a classification of t-embeddings of weighted planar bipartite graphs by positive stationary measures on the associated T-graph, and gives a reconstruction procedure.
motivation: T-graphs and t-embeddings are central combinatorial tools for studying dimer models and random tilings, but the precise correspondence between the two objects was not fully understood.
method: The authors prove a bijective-type correspondence between t-embeddings and positive stationary measures on the T-graph, describe how to reconstruct the embedding from such a measure, and use this to construct t-embeddings for sufficiently non-degenerate planar bipartite graphs.
result: t-embeddings associated with a given T-graph are classified by positive stationary measures, with an explicit reconstruction algorithm and a general existence construction.
conclusion: The work provides a probabilistic characterization of t-embeddings, opening a route to constructing them for broad classes of planar bipartite graphs.

title: Fabric Retrofit Scenario Analysis Under Uncertainty For An Urban Housing Stock Using Machine Learning
authors: Yunfei Bai, Aaron Tesfa Tsion, Ra\'ul Rosales, Barbara Shollock, Wei He
abstract: ArXiv:2610.24608v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fabric retrofit is central to decarbonising housing, and planning it depends on expected savings and their uncertainty. This study asks which upgrade saves most per dwelling and across a housing portfolio, how uncertain the savings are, and whether upgrade order matters. We propose an uncertainty-aware framework that converts predicted changes in energy performance certificate scores after wall, roof and window upgrades into standardised energy-cost savings and emission reductions. Six machine-learning models predict the 1-100 Standard Assessment Procedure (SAP) energy-cost and environmental impact (EI) emission scores from 17 certificate descriptors. Each model's errors on similar dwellings give calibrated prediction intervals. A global-best strategy applies the most accurate model throughout; a sample-specific strategy chooses each dwelling's model using these local errors. The analysis covers 103,414 officially registered dwellings in Westminster, London. CatBoost was the global-best model, with mean absolute errors of 3.487 SAP and 4.379 EI points on held-out dwellings. Both strategies projected similar savings; under global-best, roof insulation saved most per dwelling, GBP 203 annually (uncertainty range 176-229), and wall insulation most across the portfolio, GBP 6.09 million annually (uncertainty range 5.69-6.72). For 5,382 dwellings needing all three upgrades, every order delivered the same final package, yet installing roofs, walls, then windows a year apart accumulated 54% more projected cost savings over three years than the reverse order. Emission reductions followed the same pattern. Using only certificate data, the framework helps local authorities rank measures for dwellings and portfolios and sequence upgrades to bring savings forward.
tldr: A machine-learning framework estimates expected energy-cost and emission savings, with calibrated uncertainty, from fabric retrofit measures (wall, roof, window upgrades) across 103,414 dwellings in Westminster, London.
motivation: Fabric retrofit is central to decarbonising housing, but planning requires knowing which upgrades save most per dwelling and portfolio-wide, how uncertain those savings are, and whether the sequence of upgrades matters.
method: Six ML models (CatBoost best) predict SAP energy-cost and environmental-impact scores from 17 certificate descriptors, using local errors on similar dwellings to derive calibrated prediction intervals; global-best and sample-specific model-selection strategies are compared, and retrofit orderings are simulated over three years.
result: Roof insulation saved most per dwelling (GBP 203/yr, range 176-229) while wall insulation saved most across the portfolio (GBP 6.09M/yr); for 5,382 dwellings needing all three upgrades, ordering roofs-walls-windows a year apart accumulated 54% more savings over three years than the reverse order.
conclusion: Certificate-data-only uncertainty-aware frameworks can help local authorities rank and sequence retrofit measures to bring savings forward, with implications for urban decarbonisation planning.

title: Extinction And The Global Structure Of Positive Equilibria In A Ratio-dependent Intraguild Predation Model
authors: Chang-Hong Wu Tzu-Hsuan Chan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.23995v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study an intraguild predation model with ratio-dependent trophic interactions. We first derive sufficient conditions for consumer extinction, total extinction, and global convergence to biologically relevant boundary equilibria. We then turn to coexistence at equilibrium and introduce a biologically motivated coordinate transformation that reduces the positive-equilibrium problem to an explicitly parameterized one-dimensional curve. This reduction enables us to determine how the positive-equilibrium branch connects to boundary equilibria and to classify all of its admissible global geometries. We also discuss the stability of positive equilibria. Numerical examples suggest the presence of periodic and chaotic coexistence, as well as several forms of multiple attractors.
tldr: The paper analyzes extinction conditions, positive equilibria, and their global bifurcation geometry in a ratio-dependent intraguild predation model from mathematical population biology.
motivation: Intraguild predation models with ratio-dependent functional responses are ecologically important but their equilibrium structure and global behavior are not fully classified.
method: The authors derive sufficient conditions for consumer and total extinction, introduce a biologically motivated coordinate transformation that reduces the positive-equilibrium problem to a parameterized one-dimensional curve, and classify the admissible global geometries of the coexistence branch, supplemented by stability analysis and numerics.
result: The positive-equilibrium branch's connection to boundary equilibria and all admissible global geometries are classified; numerical examples indicate periodic and chaotic coexistence and multiple attractor regimes.
conclusion: The reduction technique yields a complete geometric classification of coexistence equilibria in this ratio-dependent intraguild predation model, with numerics revealing rich oscillatory and chaotic dynamics.

title: Dynamic Control Of A Make-to-Order Manufacturing System Under Throughput Time Constraints: An Effective Computational Method In The High-Dimensional Case
authors: Chun Li Baris Ata
abstract: ArXiv:2610.24096v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider dynamic control of a make-to-order production system that serves price- and delay-sensitive customers. The production system is modeled as a multiclass queueing network where the customers' delay sensitivity is modeled via throughput-time constraints. To maximize her profit while meeting these throughput time constraints, the system manager uses three different types of control: i) dynamic pricing decisions; ii) dynamic order-of-service (scheduling) decisions; and iii) outsourcing decisions upon arrival of new orders. We approximate this problem by a multi-dimensional Brownian control problem in heavy traffic, and develop a neural network-based computational method tailored for high-dimensional problems. By interpreting the solution in the context of the original model, we propose an integrated dynamic pricing, outsourcing, and scheduling policy. The effectiveness of this policy is demonstrated through a simulation study of two test problems drawn from the literature.
tldr: The paper studies dynamic pricing, scheduling, and outsourcing control for a make-to-order manufacturing system under throughput-time constraints using a high-dimensional Brownian approximation and neural-network computational method.
motivation: Managers of make-to-order production systems need to maximize profit while satisfying customer delay-sensitive throughput-time constraints through integrated pricing, scheduling, and outsourcing decisions.
method: The authors approximate the multiclass queueing network in heavy traffic by a multi-dimensional Brownian control problem and develop a neural network-based computational method for high-dimensional instances.
result: They derive an integrated dynamic pricing, outsourcing, and scheduling policy and demonstrate its effectiveness via simulation on two literature test problems.
conclusion: The proposed computational framework provides an effective dynamic control policy for high-dimensional make-to-order systems under throughput-time constraints.

title: Computing Multi-Slot First-Price Pacing Equilibria At Scale Via Entropic Smoothing
authors: Yuchen Xie, Shenyinying Tu, Yuan Gao, Yi Zhang, Deepak Kumar
abstract: ArXiv:2610.24323v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pacing equilibria describe how budget-constrained advertisers clear an ad market, but computing one at production scale is hard when every request fills several slots: the allocation jumps whenever two campaigns' scores cross. We consider the first-price pacing equilibrium (FPPE) of auctions with [MATH] homogeneous slots and unit-demand campaigns, whose Eisenberg-Gale dual reduces, via a TopK identity, to a convex program over bids. Regularizing each request's allocation with the binary (Fermi-Dirac) entropy gives a smooth, strictly convex dual whose gradient is exactly spend minus budget and whose evaluation splits into independent one-dimensional threshold solves, one per request. The smoothed equilibrium converges to the hard one at an explicit [MATH] rate, and a duality gap certifies how far any bids are from the hard equilibrium. We implement an efficient multi-GPU solver and test it on a production ad workload. We use it to compute an equilibrium price anchor: each campaign's hindsight equilibrium cost per key result.
tldr: The paper develops a smoothed convex-program formulation of multi-slot first-price pacing equilibria for ad auctions and an efficient multi-GPU solver validated on production-scale workloads.
motivation: Computing pacing equilibria at production scale is difficult because allocations jump discontinuously whenever campaign scores cross, especially when each request fills multiple slots.
method: The authors use a TopK identity to reduce the Eisenberg-Gale dual to a convex program over bids, then regularize each request's allocation with binary (Fermi-Dirac) entropy, yielding a strictly convex dual whose gradient is spend minus budget and whose evaluation decomposes into independent one-dimensional threshold solves.
result: The smoothed equilibrium converges to the hard equilibrium at an explicit rate, a duality gap certifies distance to the hard equilibrium, and the multi-GPU solver is tested on a production ad workload to compute a hindsight equilibrium price anchor.
conclusion: Entropic smoothing makes large-scale multi-slot pacing equilibrium computation tractable and practically certifiable, enabling equilibrium-based pricing benchmarks in real ad markets.

title: Asymptotic Normality Of The Hill Estimator In Linear Preferential Attachment
authors: Tiandong Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.24413v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove asymptotic normality of the Hill estimator based on the largest [MATH] degrees in a homogeneous linear preferential attachment graph with [MATH] vertices. Each new vertex sends a fixed number [MATH] of edges sequentially to older vertices, with attachment weight [MATH] and fixed [MATH]. Let [MATH]. For every deterministic sequence [MATH] satisfying [MATH], the estimator, centered at [MATH] and multiplied by [MATH], converges to a centered normal law with an explicit variance strictly smaller than [MATH]. The reduction relative to the Hill variance for independent observations separates into contributions from the different degree laws at different birth times and from competition for new edges. The contribution from competition is [MATH] times that from different birth times. Representations using Gamma and beta functions give a consistent standard error and a studentized normal limit. The proof uses martingales indexed by edge attachments and comparisons with independent pure-birth processes, while retaining the integer degrees and their ties.
tldr: The paper proves asymptotic normality of the Hill tail-index estimator computed from the largest degrees of a homogeneous linear preferential attachment graph, with an explicit variance strictly smaller than the i.i.d. Hill variance.
motivation: Heavy-tailed degree distributions arise in preferential attachment networks, and practitioners routinely apply the Hill estimator from extreme-value theory; however, its statistical guarantees were established for independent observations, not for the dependent, competition-driven degrees of a growing random graph.
method: The analysis uses martingales indexed by edge attachments and comparison arguments against independent pure-birth processes, retaining integer degrees and ties, with Gamma and beta function representations to construct a consistent standard error and a studentized limit.
result: For any deterministic sequence of top degrees satisfying the stated growth condition, the centered and scaled Hill estimator converges to a centered normal law whose variance is strictly below the i.i.d. Hill variance, with the competition contribution being a fixed multiple of the birth-time contribution.
conclusion: The work supplies valid asymptotic inference and standard errors for power-law exponent estimation in preferential attachment networks, quantifying precisely how network dependence reduces estimator variance relative to the classical i.i.d. setting.

title: A Note On The Rectangular Schoenberg-Whitney Theorem For Clamped B-splines
authors: Zixuan Zhao Shutao Tang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.24425v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wang et al.(Computer-Aided Design 40 (2008) 999-1008) proposed a knot-subsequence characterization of full row rank for rectangular B-spline collocation matrices. We identify an incorrect inequality in their Appendix proof, which invalidates the argument as written, and make explicit the endpoint and multiplicity conventions on which the criterion depends. The defect lies in the proof, not in the underlying result, which is valid under suitably stated hypotheses; in the lofting construction of Wang et al. these hypotheses are implicitly satisfied, so the lofted curves are unaffected. We state the corrected result and give a new proof, independent of the disputed argument, for clamped B-splines of arbitrary degree with continuous interior multiplicities. In our proof, sufficiency follows from inclusion of spline spaces and knot insertion; necessity selects independent columns and builds the reduced knot vector from them. The proof uses no recursive column-selection construction.
tldr: The paper corrects a flawed inequality in the Appendix proof of Wang et al.'s knot-subsequence characterization of full row rank for rectangular B-spline collocation matrices, and supplies a new independent proof for clamped B-splines of arbitrary degree.
motivation: Wang et al. (2008) gave a knot-subsequence criterion for full row rank of rectangular B-spline collocation matrices, but their Appendix argument contains an incorrect inequality, leaving the criterion without a valid proof.
method: The authors identify the erroneous step, make explicit the endpoint and clamped-multiplicity conventions the criterion relies on, and construct a new proof in which sufficiency follows from spline-space inclusion plus knot insertion and necessity proceeds by selecting independent columns and building the reduced knot vector.
result: The underlying rank criterion is confirmed valid under suitably stated hypotheses, with the defect confined to the proof; a self-contained, non-recursive proof is established for clamped B-splines of arbitrary degree with continuous interior multiplicities.
conclusion: The result is a self-contained numerical-analysis correction with no impact on the lofting constructions of Wang et al., whose hypotheses implicitly satisfy the required conditions.

title: Asymptotics For The Number Of Saddle Connections On A Slit Torus
authors: Howard Masur David Aulicino
abstract: ArXiv:2610.24429v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a flat torus with a marked line segment [MATH] and prove linear asymptotics for closed curves on the torus disjoint from the interior of the line segment. We also consider segments that begin and terminate at the end points of [MATH] whose interiors are disjoint from [MATH] and prove [MATH] asymptotics. In all cases, after quotienting by the growth rate, we compute the constant explicitly, which differs depending on whether or not [MATH] lies in a periodic direction on the torus. In particular, when [MATH] lies along a non-periodic trajectory, we show the constant is [MATH]. Moreover, we prove that as a function of the holonomy vector of [MATH], the constants are continuous at the points where [MATH] lies in a non-periodic direction.
tldr: The paper establishes linear and quadratic asymptotics, with explicit constants, for counting saddle connections and closed curves on a flat torus slit along a marked line segment.
motivation: Counting saddle connections on flat surfaces is a central problem in Teichmüller dynamics; the authors aim to extend known asymptotic counting results to the simple but non-trivial case of a torus with a slit.
method: Using techniques from flat surface geometry and translation surface theory, the authors count closed geodesics disjoint from the slit and segments connecting the slit endpoints, then quotient by the growth rate to extract explicit constants via the holonomy vector of the slit.
result: Linear asymptotics are proven for closed curves avoiding the slit and quadratic asymptotics for endpoint-to-endpoint segments; the constants are computed explicitly, depend on whether the slit lies in a periodic direction, and equal a specific value in the non-periodic case.
conclusion: The constants vary continuously as functions of the holonomy vector, including at non-periodic directions, providing a precise quantitative picture of saddle connection growth on slit tori.

title: Riemannian Submersion Whose Total Manifold Admits An Almost Hyperbolic Ricci Soliton
authors: Sonali Jaiswal, Akhilesh Yadav, S. S. Shukla
abstract: ArXiv:2610.24488v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the present paper, we investigate geometric properties of a Riemannian submersion for which the total manifold is endowed with hyperbolic and almost hyperbolic Ricci solitons. We establish conditions under which the fibers of the submersion admit hyperbolic and almost hyperbolic Ricci solitons. Further, we derive necessary conditions for the base manifold to be an Einstein and a hyperbolic Ricci soliton. Also, we determine the scalar curvature associated with the fibers and the base manifold. Moreover, when the total space admits an almost hyperbolic Ricci soliton with a torse-forming potential vector field, we obtain conditions ensuring that the extrinsic vertical and horizontal distributions are almost generalized quasi-Einstein. We also obtain necessary conditions for the fibers and base manifold to be an Einstein and almost generalized quasi-Einstein manifold. Finally, examples are included to illustrate the existence of hyperbolic and almost hyperbolic Ricci solitons in Riemannian submersion.
tldr: A pure differential-geometry study of Riemannian submersions whose total space carries hyperbolic or almost hyperbolic Ricci soliton structures.
motivation: Ricci solitons generalize Einstein metrics and are of interest in geometric analysis and the study of Ricci flow; the authors extend this machinery to the setting of Riemannian submersions.
method: The authors derive conditions on the fibers, base manifold, and vertical/horizontal distributions under which hyperbolic and almost hyperbolic Ricci soliton structures descend or persist, including the case of a torse-forming potential vector field, and compute scalar curvatures.
result: Sufficient and necessary conditions are obtained for fibers and base manifolds to be Einstein or almost generalized quasi-Einstein, together with explicit scalar curvature expressions, and examples of such solitons in submersions are constructed.
conclusion: The work characterizes how hyperbolic Ricci soliton geometry behaves under Riemannian submersions, providing a structural toolkit for constructing such metrics on fibered spaces.

title: Locally Convex Spaces With Hemicompact Weak* Dual
authors: Evgenii Reznichenko
abstract: ArXiv:2610.24615v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a locally convex space [MATH] let [MATH] denote its dual endowed with the weak* topology [MATH]. We prove that [MATH] is hemicompact if and only if [MATH] with the Mackey topology [MATH] is metrizable and barrelled, and if and only if [MATH] is [MATH]-compact and quasi-complete. The key step is that a hemicompact [MATH] is quasi-complete. The Mackey topology [MATH] is metrizable if and only if [MATH] is a countable union of absolutely convex weak*-compact sets; spaces with normable barrelled Mackey topology are characterized similarly. As a consequence, a metrizable (in particular, normed) space [MATH] is barrelled if and only if [MATH] is hemicompact. For function spaces we obtain: [MATH] is hemicompact if and only if [MATH] is hemicompact, and [MATH] is hemicompact if and only if [MATH] is countable and all compact subsets of [MATH] are finite.
tldr: A pure functional-analysis paper characterizing when the weak* dual of a locally convex space is hemicompact, via Mackey-topology metrizability and barrelledness conditions.
motivation: Hemicompactness of duals with weak* topology is a basic topological property whose structural characterization in terms of Mackey topology and quasi-completeness was not fully settled.
method: Abstract locally convex space arguments: showing hemicompact weak*-duals are quasi-complete, relating metrizability of the Mackey topology to countable unions of absolutely convex weak*-compact sets, and specializing to function spaces.
result: Weak* dual hemicompact iff Mackey topology is metrizable and barrelled iff the dual is k-compact and quasi-complete; metrizable spaces are barrelled iff their dual is hemicompact, with analogous characterizations for C_p and C_k function spaces.
conclusion: Provides a clean topological characterization linking hemicompactness of the weak* dual to metrizability, barrelledness and quasi-completeness, with corollaries for normed and function spaces.

title: ToolRosetta: Surface-Form Invariance Of Tool-Call Guards
authors: Jens Ernstberger Hasan Demirkiran
abstract: ArXiv:2610.24055v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Step-level guards for tool-using agents are evaluated on tidy JSON tool calls, but deployed coding agents act through execute_bash and execute_code tools whose payloads are strings. We introduce ToolRosetta, which re-renders every candidate action in the AgentDojo and AgentHarm splits of TS-Bench as a Python call, as a shell command, and without the agent's rationale. The renderings are produced by code and verified by round-trip parsing, so the user request, the history, the label and the action's effect stay fixed while only the surface form changes. Across eleven guards with two placebo controls, frontier and strong open-weight guards are stable: no frontier error rate moves by more than 3.4 points. Four of five specialized agent guards are not: under the shell form their false-positive rates rise by 21 to 47 points on AgentDojo, and TS-Guard's by 38 points on its own home benchmark, blocking between a third and nine in ten benign actions; the fifth, StepGuard, does not move. A small open guard drifts five points more permissive. Removing the agent's rationale moves most guards whose input carries it, in guard-specific directions. A request-blind control on one guard shows that the rationale is where intent is read from. A parser that restores the canonical call in front of the guard removes the effect for these renderings, by construction. Benchmark accuracy on JSON calls does not predict a guard's operating point behind a code-acting agent.
tldr: ToolRosetta tests whether step-level safety guards for tool-using LLM agents remain reliable when the same action is re-rendered as Python calls or shell commands rather than canonical JSON.
motivation: Deployed coding agents act through execute_bash and execute_code with string payloads, yet guard models are benchmarked on tidy JSON tool calls, so benchmark accuracy may not predict real operating points.
method: The authors re-render every candidate action in the AgentDojo and AgentHarm splits of TS-Bench as a Python call, a shell command, and without the agent's rationale, using code generation with round-trip parsing verification to hold request, history, label and effect fixed while varying only surface form; eleven guards plus two placebo controls are evaluated.
result: Frontier and strong open-weight guards move by at most 3.4 points, but four of five specialized agent guards degrade sharply — false-positive rates rise 21–47 points under shell form on AgentDojo and 38 points for TS-Guard on its home benchmark, blocking a third to nine in ten benign actions, while StepGuard is unaffected.
conclusion: JSON benchmark accuracy does not predict a guard's operating point behind a code-acting agent; surface-form invariance and rationale-independence are necessary properties for guard evaluation, and a canonicalizing parser removes the effect by construction.

title: Under The Skin: Backdoor Infection In Multimodal Large Language Models
authors: Jiawen Wang, Ruo Yang, Haoran Dai, Binghui Wang, Ning Luo
abstract: ArXiv:2610.24058v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have achieved impressive performance in generating text conditioned on inputs from different modalities. In this work, we introduce backdoor infection, a cross-modal attack framework targeting MLLMs. Starting from a model already injected with a backdoor in one modality, our attack constructs a corresponding trigger in another modality, called the infected modality. Exploiting the model's shared latent space, the trigger in the infected modality reliably activates the malicious behavior, without modifying or poisoning the infected modality during training. We further develop a lightweight, constraint-aware optimization method for efficient and practical trigger generation.
